qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Dario's band spent months writing a song for the spring showcase. When they played it for his sister, she granted that the melody sounded like nothing she had ever heard on the radio -- but the lyrics, she said, were the problem: phrase after phrase that no one had ever used before, and that still managed to say nothing at all. No story, no feeling, no idea anywhere. What is his sister saying about the song?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: That it is vapid, completely empty of thought or meaning despite being new.
That it is trite, built from stock phrases gone stale through years of overuse.
That it is banal, a dull recycling of ideas listeners have heard many times before.
That it is humdrum, the boring sameness of one routine repeated day after day.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. The sister's complaint is emptiness: the words are new, but there is no story, no feeling, no idea in them. A lyric completely empty of thought or meaning is vapid.

Not quite. She says the melody sounds like nothing on the radio and the phrases have never been used before -- so the song is not recycled, not worn stale, and not a repeated routine. Words that are brand new and still say nothing at all are vapid.

Trite describes language drained of life by constant overuse -- it was fresh once, and repetition wore it out. These lyrics were never anyone else's: the sister says no one has used the phrases before. Words cannot be worn out on their first outing; her complaint is their emptiness.

Banal means dull, commonplace, and unoriginal -- ideas heard many times before. But the sister grants that the melody is unlike anything on the radio and that the phrases are ones no one has used. Her charge is not that the song copies; it is that the song, original as it is, contains no thought at all -- and empty of thought is vapid.

Humdrum is the boring sameness of routine -- the same commute, the same chores, day after day. The sister heard this song exactly once, and her objection is to what the lyrics fail to say, not to any repetition.
